before.lead: Ordering an item from a shop and asking it to personalize something you already own can require different first steps. I help Lexington and Fayette County businesses explain those routes before customers choose a design or request a quote.
before.decisionTitle: Identify the item before approving its personalization.
before.decision: For an illustrative engraving business, a design choice does not establish that a customer-supplied object is suitable for the work. The Lexington example below explicitly invites customers to bring an item, send a photograph or describe a project. I can clarify the difference between shop-supplied products and supplied-item inquiries around an existing contact route, or build a fuller service introduction. The owner determines what can be accepted; the website should preserve that review before presenting the requested personalization as agreed work.

scopes.title: Separate product orders and supplied-item inquiries
scopes.request: Make it clear whether the customer is choosing an offered product or asking about an object they already have. Use the business’s approved way to begin that discussion.
scopes.supplies: The products you supply, the kinds of supplied-item inquiries you consider and the information your team uses to assess them.
scopes.check: A customer with their own cup can ask about that item without being treated as though they selected a product from your catalog. Spelling approval does not stand in for item acceptance.

scopes.title: Build a service and product introduction
scopes.request: Explain the two routes with approved examples and a clear account of what happens next. Keep any functioning shop or order provider connected to the appropriate product choices.
scopes.supplies: Accurate service limits, approved photographs and current descriptions of the work the business accepts.
scopes.check: Visitors understand who is supplying the object and which review comes next. A displayed engraving example is not an assurance that every material or object can be accepted.

before.question: How can I check what I receive at website handoff?
before.answer: Check the source and content files, approved assets, dependency and non-secret configuration files, licenses, account inventory, completed checks and build and publishing instructions. The delivery should identify unfinished items too. Paid files arrive within five business days after the work is finished or the account is settled if it stops early; they do not wait for the correction period.

before.question: What if a review finds that the missing form details cannot be fixed safely?
before.answer: The review still provides findings, access limits and an ordered list of next steps. A small included fix is conditional on being safe and practical; it is not a promise to repair any form or provider. If resolving the fault requires broader changes, I describe that work and agree on a separate price before proceeding.

after.question: How can I check what I receive at website handoff?
after.answer: You receive the paid website files, publishing instructions and a record of completed checks and unfinished items. Use the linked handoff checklist to inspect the full delivery. before.question: Can you improve our wood photographs without misrepresenting the material?
before.answer: I can prepare supplied photographs for clear website use, with the edits agreed in the written proposal. We should preserve the grain, weathering and other details the example is meant to show, and explain relevant lighting or sample differences in the caption. Screens cannot guarantee an exact color match. You approve the images and factual descriptions; new photography is separate work.
